title: Maps, Globes, and the Earth's Grid

questions.question: Which line of latitude divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern hemispheres?
questions.rationale: The Equator (0° latitude) divides the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres; the Prime Meridian divides longitude.

questions.question: The Prime Meridian passes through:
questions.rationale: The Prime Meridian (0° longitude) passes through Greenwich, England; its opposite is roughly the International Date Line at 180°.

questions.question: A city map with scale 1:10,000 is best described as:
options: A small-scale map showing a large area
A large-scale map showing a small area in detail
questions.rationale: Large-scale maps (like 1:10,000) cover small areas with great detail — a city plan. Small-scale maps show large areas with less detail.

questions.question: Which map element explains the meaning of symbols and colours used on the map?
questions.rationale: The legend (or key) defines what each symbol and colour on the map represents.

questions.question: About what fraction of Earth's surface is covered by water?
questions.rationale: Roughly 71% of Earth's surface is water and about 29% is land.

questions.question: Latitude measures distance north or south of the Equator in degrees within which range?
questions.rationale: Latitude runs from 0° at the Equator to 90° at the poles; longitude is the one measured in degrees 0°–180° east or west of the Prime Meridian.

questions.question: Which line of latitude marks the northern limit of the Sun's direct rays?
questions.rationale: The Tropic of Cancer at 23.5° N is the northern limit of the Sun's direct rays; the Tropic of Capricorn at 23.5° S is the southern limit.

questions.question: The 180° meridian roughly coincides with which line?
questions.rationale: The 180° meridian roughly coincides with the International Date Line, opposite the Prime Meridian at 0°.

questions.question: Which map element shows the ratio between map distance and real-world distance?
questions.rationale: The scale expresses the ratio between distance on the map and the corresponding real distance; direction comes from a north arrow or compass rose.

questions.question: A map that focuses on one theme such as rainfall or population density is classified as:
questions.rationale: Thematic maps focus on a single theme such as climate, population, or economic activity; physical maps show natural features and political maps show boundaries and cities.

questions.question: According to the lesson, Earth's shape is best described as:
options: Geoid — an oblate spheroid flattened at the poles
An egg-shaped body bulging at the poles
questions.rationale: Earth is described as a Geoid — an oblate spheroid flattened at the poles — with an equatorial circumference of about 40,075 km.
